A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FixMatch/SA-FixMatch study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Appendices A–K can be matched across versions; v2 additionally contains Appendix L. No essential comparison gaps remain.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments, Grad-CAM comparisons, mask-size ablations, and augmentation experiments in Section 5 and Appendix K.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a comparison using the same training images for SL, FixMatch, and SA-FixMatch in Section 5.4.

M1.justification: The network, supervised and unsupervised losses, pseudo-labeling procedure, and Grad-CAM-based SA-CutOut remain unchanged. Section 4.3 and Appendix J retain the same algorithm; the added experiment changes data access rather than the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-100, STL-10, Imagewoof, and ImageNet. The new comparison restricts training-image access within existing benchmarks, without adding a task or population. Appendix L supplies illustrative examples rather than new evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: SL and FixMatch remain the comparators for SA-FixMatch. The FlexMatch, FreeMatch, Dash, and SoftMatch comparisons are retained unchanged in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2. The added control uses existing comparators; newly cited feature-learning methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds an equal-image control on STL-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, with labeled and unlabeled pools containing the same images. Appendix K.5 specifies 50 epochs and 102,400 iterations for this experiment. The original benchmark protocol remains at 150 epochs and 307,200 iterations.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds a controlled comparison testing whether the methods' advantages persist without access to additional unlabeled images. The existing mask-size, weak-augmentation, strong-augmentation, CutOut, and Grad-CAM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times and report means and standard deviations. Existing uncertainty values are retained. The new control table gives point estimates, as existing ablation tables already did; no new seed information, uncertainty procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 Table 3 adds results for the equal-image protocol. For example, with 40 STL-10 training images, SL, FixMatch, and SA-FixMatch achieve 19.93%, 38.88%, and 40.25%, respectively. Original benchmark scores, merged from v1 Tables 1–2 into v2 Table 1, and existing supplementary results are unchanged. The added scores concern different conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix A changes the smoothed-ReLU definition from q ≥ 2 to q ≥ 3, aligning it with the existing parameter assumption. Induction Hypothesis 15(d) changes its lower bound from Ω(σ0) to tilde-Ω(σ0). Appendix E.3 also removes its opening sample-size justification. The principal theorems and proof framework remain; most other mathematical edits rename symbols.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: explaining FixMatch's generalization through more complete feature learning, extending the analysis to related SSL methods, and proposing SA-FixMatch. Rewording and additional supporting evidence do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly argues that SA-FixMatch's analysis remains applicable when labeled and unlabeled datasets contain the same images, attributing this to deterministic removal of learned features. Section 4.2 adds a connection to consistency regularization in self-supervised pretraining. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix K.5 adds the training budget for the new equal-image experiment: 50 epochs with 2,048 iterations per epoch. Existing hardware, optimizer settings, image and mask sizes, SA-CutOut timing, and implementation-source information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a feature-learning paragraph and four references: Allen-Zhu and Li (2022), Wen and Li (2021, 2022), and Park et al. (2018). This contextualizes the work relative to adversarial training, self-supervised learning, and adversarial dropout while retaining its existing novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 polishes wording across the introduction, setup, and results, standardizes terminology and proof notation, and updates author information. It adds acknowledgments and Appendix L's explanation of the multi-view assumption. The main narrative sequence and proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 merges the original benchmark Tables 1–2 into a denser Table 1, renumbers the SSL-variant comparison, and adds Table 3 beside the mask-size table. It adds Figure 5's car examples and conference headers. Figures 1–4 retain their image content, with some relocation.

improvement.justification: The new equal-image control in Section 5.4 provides useful evidence that the advantages persist without a larger unlabeled image pool, strengthening v1's experimental support. Appendix L and focused explanatory and mathematical corrections improve clarity. These are incremental gains: the central theory and original results remain, while the new control reports only point estimates and the merged benchmark table is less readable.
